fatal_errors: The proposed Cu@Gr addition and spark-plasma sintering do not reconstruct the target intervention of liquid-metal dealloying a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
The initial material is treated as a conventional W–Cu composite rather than the nominally equiatomic, single-BCC WTaVTi dendrite–interdendrite precursor.
The proposed interfacial graphene mediator is inconsistent with the target W-rich passivating interlayer and selective Ti–Cu exchange mechanism.
No cited evidence supports improved behavior under irradiation; the evidence only supports SPS densification and room-temperature transport improvements.
The service claim is generalized to fusion irradiation without specifying or reproducing the target's limited 25 keV He+ blistering-screen conditions.
explanation: This is a literature-supported alternative for improving conventional W–Cu composites, but it is not a reconstruction of the hidden study. Evidence E2 and E3 directly supports 0.8 wt.% Cu@Gr-assisted SPS, enhanced densification, continuous Cu pathways, and an approximately 24.3% thermal-conductivity increase. However, the generated mechanism overstates graphene as a stable interfacial barrier: the cited work instead emphasizes graphene-assisted activated sintering, liquid-Cu redistribution, and tungsten-carbide formation. The hypothesis also extrapolates to irradiation performance without supporting data. Its controlled doped-versus-undoped experiment is reasonably falsifiable, although irradiation dose, energy, temperature, and failure metrics are insufficiently defined. It misses the target's WTaVTi precursor, 1200 °C/96 h liquid-metal dealloying, selective removal of Ti-rich channels, bicontinuous RHEA–Cu architecture, W-rich interlayer, temperature-dependent thermal crossover, and proxy He-irradiation comparison against pure W.
